articles.title: Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare Preview - Experience the Lovecraftian Side of the Marvel Universe
articles.summary: We've got an exclusive preview of Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare, a psychedelic journey into the Lovecraftian side of the Marvel Universe.
articles.body:
Abrams ComicArts is debuting the latest in its ongoing MarvelArts series of original graphic novels. This time, the focus is on the Sorcerer Supreme as he battles foes both iconic and obscure in Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare.

With Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare in stores now, IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of this epic, psychedelic graphic novel. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare Preview Gallery

Doctor Strange: Endless Nightmare reunites the creative team behind Dune: The Official Graphic Novel , including writer Kevin J. Anderson and artists Raúl Allén and Patricia Martín. Here's the official summary of the book:

When Stephen Strange encounters a mysterious patient at his hospital who won’t stop raving about how life is “nothing but the dream of a sleeping god,” the rest of the world is suddenly struck with insomnia. In order to prevent chaos from unfolding as the people around him become more and more desperate for sleep, Doctor Strange must embark into the mind of the madman who seems to have heralded this disaster, taking a psychedelic trip into the Nightmare Realm.

“The character of Doctor Strange has access to so many bizarre realms, I wanted to introduce him to a dark and twisted Lovecraft-inspired story.” said Anderson in a statement. “I brought in an important and popular villain in the Doctor Strange universe, as well as another villain who has never appeared since Stan Lee and Steve Ditko created him in 1964’s Dr. Strange #122. It was amazing to play in this universe.”

articles.title: The White House pulls its racist Tetris clone
articles.summary: The White House has removed its racist Tetris clone “Build the Wall” days after launching its “arcade.”
articles.body: The White House has taken down its racist Tetris ripoff days after launching a website dedicated to “arcade games,” as spotted earlier by Kotaku. The Tetris clone, called “Build the Wall,” involved stacking different-sized blocks to prevent a “zombie border siege.” It’s not clear why the White House removed the title, though the Tetris Company previously said that it’s looking into the situation. “For more than 40 years, Tetris has brought people together across generations and cultures through play and joy,” Tetris spokesperson Kerri Brusca told The Verge last week. “The objective of the game has always been to stack with purpose to clear as many lines as possible. We are currently reviewing the matter.” The Verge reached out to the Tetris Company with a request for comment but didn’t immediately hear back. Other “games” that align with President Donald Trump’s agenda are still available on the White House’s website, including the Flappy Bird ripoff “Flappy Bill,” a Tapper-like game called “Supply Line,” “Trump Savings Tycoon,” and “Rio Run.”

articles.title: Practical Magic 2 Brings Back Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, But It's Cursed With a Very Messy Script
articles.summary: Sandra Bullock, Nicole Kidman and the rest of the Practical Magic 2 cast toil and trouble to conjure up a worthwhile sequel, but they’re cursed with a very messy script.
articles.body:
Practical Magic 2 is in theaters on September 11.

In 1998, director Griffin Dunne, along with Bullock and Kidman, delivered the equivalent of a warm autumnal Wiccan hug of a movie with Practical Magic . A modest hit at the box office, its power grew over the years as a cult favorite because of the luminous charm of the two leads as love-lorn, cursed witch sisters Sally and Gillian Owens.

Twenty-eight years later, it’s actually a little bit of Hollywood magic that Practical Magic 2 even got made with the returning cast of Bullock, Kidman, Stockard Channing, and Dianne Wiest as the matriarchs of the Owens family, all still residing together in their family home in Massachusetts. As beguiling as it is to see the return of these actresses, their alchemy is impeded by a hyperactive screenplay that’s too busy bouncing them through plot beats and muddled stakes instead of giving them, and the new cast, better stories.

Practical Magic 2 adapts from author Alice Hoffman’s novel series about the Owens clan of witches, this time primarily drawing from 2021’s The Book of Magic. It’s about 20-ish years since the end of the first film, which had the Owens witches “outing” themselves on Halloween to their little town, publicly embracing their Wiccan legacy.

Today, Bullock’s Sally is the town librarian and dedicated single mother to grown daughters Kylie (Joey King) and neurosurgeon-in-training Antonia (Maisie Williams). Because of the still intact 300-year-old Owens curse that brings death to any man to whom they confess their love, Sally has kept her girls in the dark about their magical abilities. She’s made her still free-spirited yet vaguely employed sister Gilly (Kidman) promise not to tell them, along with the reluctant buy-in of their aunts, Jet (Weist) and Franny (Channing).

But time and curses can only be held at bay for so long, and Kylie’s serious relationship with earnest Gideon (Xolo Maridueña) and the chirping of a deathwatch beetle means heartbreak and a lot of secrets are going to spill at the same time. The intersection of a curse-induced accident and Jet finding a long-hidden tome, The Book of the Raven (written by their ancestor and curse creator Maria Owens), prompts a dramatic breach in the family. A livid Kylie lays out her mother for hiding their magical abilities all their lives, and proceeds to impulsively listen to a beckoning voice compelling her to England, where it promises a way to save Gideon’s life. A road trip ensues with a panicked Sally engaging Gillian to follow, while looking up a UK expert, Dr. Ian Wright (Lee Pace), for help in unlocking the secrets of the Owens book and the history of Maria’s birthplace.

In theory, it’s not a bad idea to shake up the single locale dynamics of the first movie and dig into the family history. However, the screenplay by Akiva Goldsman, Georgia Pritchett and Kelly Marcel sacrifices the insular charm and Wiccan history of the Massachusetts community for an odd-couple travel comedy featuring the still oil-and-water sisters. Sally has been, and remains for the majority of this film, in emotional stasis, too broken and closed down from repeated losses. Thankfully, Bullock still knows how to make an audience feel the pain of her character. But there’s also a strong sense that the script is wasting the broader talents of what Bullock could have brought to her character rather than give her a one-note trajectory that you see coming a mile away.

Kidman does her impish best to play Gillian as the devil on Sally’s shoulder, trying to break those tall emotional walls while pushing her towards the very handsome and multi-tattooed Dr. Wright. But outside of playing her frustrated sister’s keeper, the script shorts the actress any parallel meaty story like she had with the murder of Gilly’s truly frightening ex-boyfriend Jimmy (Goran Visnjic) in the first film. When Bullock and Kidman get some rare quiet moments to just let the sisters talk, they make the most of it every time. But those moments are few and far between the more the chase for Kylie picks up and gets burdened with an overly convoluted exposition dump about the ancient history of the area where Maria was burned to death, and who or what has been summoning Kylie.

As for Pace, I’ll never understand how an actor as charming and compelling as he is gets handed such underwhelming material. If you can’t write a character for the man that is clearly swoon-worthy from the get-go, you’re doing something incredibly wrong. In fact, it’s a little insulting that Wright is introduced in a stunt set piece that frames him purely as eye candy, with little clarity of purpose aside from playing a potential love interest. And even then, the script gives Bullock and Pace scenes with so much tonal whiplash it’s never clear if they’re actually flirting, or just being passive-aggressive with one another. The heat and charm found between Sally and Aidan Quinn’s Detective Gary Hallet in the first film is sorely missing between Sally and Wright no matter how hard the actors try, and that's a big problem in getting the audience to buy the power of love.

The film’s other cardinal sin is separating the main cast, with Bullock, Kidman, Pace and King essentially in their own mini chase movie in picturesque, tax-incentivized England. Director Susanne Bier doesn’t frame the locations or set pieces with much scale or even the fairy-tale charm that Dunne shot the first film with, so the sequel lacks the mood and menace that gave the original such memorable vibes. Meanwhile, Channing, Williams and Maridueña are stuck back home in what feels like a single-room loaner hospital set from a soap opera. In particular, Williams is done dirty, given nothing of note to do, which is a travesty. Ageism also looms with Weist and Channing, who are relegated to cliché fates that work as well as they do only because of both women’s immense talent for wringing the most out of any scene they appear in.

I was also particularly disappointed that Alan Silvestri’s score from Practical Magic, so essential in creating the tone of the original, is only gently alluded to in Rupert Gregson-Williams’ original score. Instead, Bier and company lean on other nostalgic reprises that just don’t have the same weight or impact as Silvestri’s themes.

Though Practical Magic 2 isn’t a terrible second chapter, one is left at the end with the feeling that a much better sequel, with more deeply considered and well-crafted versions of the Owens women, might be floating somewhere out there in the winds above Massachusetts.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gameplay Revealed! - IGN
articles.summary: Get a closer look at gameplay from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake in this latest video for the upcoming remake of the 1998 adventure game. This new gameplay video, led by series producer Eiji Aonuma, showcases Kokiri Village, Hyrule Field, and Hyrule Castle Town. We get to see new, overhauled visuals with reimagined graphics, and new mechanics, including the ability to rotate the camera, jumps which are now done via button presses versus automatically in the original game, dashing, and the addition of new dialogue. We also get a look at dungeon gameplay in the Great Deku Tree, throwing Deku nuts and using the slingshot item to solve puzzles and fight enemies. New features also show that time no longer stops in towns, and day and night cycles will continue. You can also hum songs Link has learned that will play on the Ocarina, and the game will also react to instruments. Additionally, a new feature is Threads of Time, where you can see progress you've made in your story and check your next objective.The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will be available on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026.

articles.summary: This convertible weighs only one pound more than a handheld gaming PC.
articles.body:
For this week only, Best Buy is offering a major price drop on a compact convertible laptop that doubles as a gaming powerhouse. The diminutive Asus ROG Flow Z13 gaming laptop with 64GB of RAM is now available for just $2,099.99 with free shipping after a massive $900 off discount. The Asus Flow Z13 (in tablet mode) is only a pound heavier than the ROG Ally X20 handheld gaming PC , but offers more versatility and better gaming performance that rivals full-sized laptops.

Save $900 Off an 2.65-Pound Asus ROG Flow Z13 Gaming Laptop

Asus ROG Flow Z13 13.4" 2.5K Touch-Screen AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S) Gaming Laptop with 64GB RAM

The Asus ROG Flow Z13 is a 13.4" 2-in-1 convertible laptop that weighs in at only 2.65 pounds in tablet mode. That's about one pound heavier than the Xbox Ally X handheld, which weighs in at 1.6 pounds. A premium laptop deserves premium build quality, and the Flow Z13 doesn't disappoint with a blacked out CNC aluminum alloy chassis and Corning Gorilla Glass Victus screen protection. The keyboard can be detached so that the Z13 can be used as a tablet.

This particular configuration is equipped with a 13.4" 2560x1600 180Hz IPS display, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 CPU with AMD Radeon 8060S iGPU, 64GB of LPDDR5X-8000Mhz RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Radeon 8060S is a technological marvel of an iGPU. It's far and away the most powerful integrated graphics solution on the market and nearly the same gaming performance as a discrete RTX 5060 mobile (faster than an RTX 4060 mobile). It's considerably more powerful than the Ryzen Z2 Extreme APU found in the highest-end handheld gaming PCs like the ROG Xbox Ally X or Legion Go 2.

IGN's Chris Coke reviewed this laptop and was extremely impressed at how well it ran even the most demanding games despite its diminutive size. Our test sample had 32GB of RAM and was priced at $2,300. You're getting double the RAM for a lower price. Because the RAM is soldered onto the board, there's no chance to upgrade the memory capacity. That's why the 64GB of RAM preinstalled on this particular configuration is a welcome addition. RAM prices are still at an all-time high, so the fact that there's a steep discount on such a loaded system makes this deal even better than it seems.

articles.title: Nintendo isn’t scared of GTA VI
articles.summary: Most game publishers are getting out of the way of Grand Theft Auto 6, but Nintendo is going up against it with the next Zelda on the Switch 2.
articles.body: There’s never really been a game like Grand Theft Auto VI before, one that has completely altered the lineup of games around it. Everyone, it seems, is scared of going up against Grand Theft Auto VI. Everyone, that is, except for Nintendo. The company held a 30-minute showcase this morning focused entirely on its Legend of Zelda franchise, which is celebrating its 40th anniversary. We got a title for the live-action movie, a series of orchestral concerts, and a very glittery special edition of the Switch 2. But most of the runtime was dedicated to the upcoming Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time. There was a new trailer and a lengthy gameplay video that showed how Nintendo is approaching this remake, which includes more realistic graphics and new features like a free camera. But perhaps the most notable detail is when the game launches: November 5th. Grand Theft Auto VI, if you’re unaware, launches on November 19th. It’s a date that has caused a seismic shift in the video game release calendar as virtually every major publisher has either delayed games or moved their release dates up in order to avoid GTA and the all-encompassing vacuum it creates. September just began, and already we’ve had launches like Star Wars Zero Company, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, with heavy hitters like Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, and a remastered Witcher 3 coming later in the month. [Image: It’s a similar situation to the surprise launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong last year, where indie games jumped out of the way of its release. But GTA VI exists on a much larger scale. With few exceptions — including a pair of brave indies — publishers have decided that it’s better to be caught in a glut of releases in September than go up against GTA VI later in the year. In fact, Ocarina of Time is the only other major release that isn’t a port and is currently slated for November. Of course, it’s not really all that surprising that Nintendo isn’t afraid of competing with GTA VI. In some ways, the games aren’t competing directly at all; Ocarina of Time will be a Switch 2 exclusive, while GTA is coming to the Xbox and PS5. But there’s more to it than that. Zelda and GTA will still be fighting over cultural mindshare, which is something that both Nintendo and Rockstar have become adept at cultivating. And they’ve both done it largely the same way: by ignoring what everyone else is doing. For Rockstar, the massive success of GTA V allowed the studio the space and freedom to do essentially whatever it wanted, and the decade-plus in between Grand Theft Auto releases has generated a level of hype that has perhaps never been seen before in any entertainment industry. That has allowed the next game to largely exist in its own universe, where Rockstar can do unprecedented things like put out a lengthy gameplay video on Netflix. [Media: Nintendo operates in a similar way, largely following its own whims rather than industry trends. This has led to some high-profile failures — RIP to the Wii U — but over the last decade or so, Nintendo has further distanced itself from competitors Sony and Microsoft, going in a completely new direction with its hybrid Switch line of hardware. Instead of following trends, Nintendo now starts them: Just look at all of the devices that followed the Switch, from the Steam Deck to the PlayStation Portal. The PS6 might even be a portable. If you want a clear example of just how separate Nintendo is from the rest of the industry, look no further than 2020. In the same week that the PS5 and Xbox Series X were ushering in the next generation of game consoles, Nintendo also launched its own hardware: an updated version of the Game & Watch that could play Super Mario Bros. and tell you the time. It’s hard to get much further away from next-gen than that. The current iteration of Nintendo is one that largely avoids risks and often plays things safe. But it’s also one that operates with an incredible amount of confidence, which is something that much of the rest of the industry lacks, at least when it comes to GTA. The next Grand Theft Auto may have the ability to warp the video game release calendar, but Nintendo and Zelda have enough pull to be able to ignore it.

articles.title: South Park Trolls Trump, Google, and Apple With Official Season 29 Name Change
articles.summary: South Park is officially changing its name for the launch of Season 29 as creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone troll Apple, Google, and of course U.S. president Donald Trump.
articles.body:
South Park is officially changing its name for the launch of Season 29 as creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone troll Apple, Google, and of course U.S. President Donald Trump.

Season 29, which premieres Wednesday, September 16 at 10pm ET / PT on Comedy Central and the next day on Paramount+, brings with it a big change. Here’s the statement from Parker and Stone:

“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA. We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount -- a Skydance Capitulation."

That’s a clear joke about U.S. President Donald Trump’s ongoing attempts to rename different parts of the world in his image, and tech companies going along with it. Earlier this month, Apple renamed Lake Ontario as Lake America on its Maps app, after an order from Trump as part of Washington's trade spat with Canada. Google made a similar switch for its users in the U.S., sparking a backlash.

Trump had posted several AI-generated videos on social media, including a clip of him kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with another that says "Welcome to Lake America.”

In 2025, Google re-designated the Gulf of Mexico after Trump declared it would be called the Gulf of America. Mexico sued Google over it.

Expect a six-episode season, with new episodes dropping every two weeks (September 30, October 14, October 28, November 11, November 25).

Season 28 came to an end in December after a number of controversial episodes that sparked responses from the White House. Its overarching story saw Donald Trump try and fail to convince Satan not to go through with having their ‘butt baby,’ aka the Antichrist. Vice president J.D. Vance even conspired with Trump to try to murder the baby.

South Park abruptly brought Season 27 to an end after just five episodes, and Season 28 ended after the same number. With Season 29 running six episodes, perhaps Season 30 will kick off early 2027.

Traditionally, Parker and Stone create each episode week by week, which makes for a chaotic production but topical shows. Comedy Central had delayed the Season 27-ender just hours before it was due to air, with Parker and Stone insisting the blame lay at their door . “Apparently when you do everything at the last minute sometimes you don’t get it done,” the pair told Variety . “This one’s on us. We didn’t get it done in time. Thanks to Comedy Central and South Park fans for being so understanding. Tune in next week!” As far as we at IGN are aware, Parker and Stone had missed the scheduled release of South Park just once before, due to a power outage, but never for not getting an episode done in time.

It’s worth noting that during their San Diego Comic-Con 2025 panel , which took place the day after the Donald Trump-skewering Season 27 opener aired, Parker said he and Stone were unsure what the next episode would be, revealing the decision was “super stressful.” It roasted Trump to such an extent that it sparked a rebuttal from the White House. Parker and Stone have said they were attracted to “new taboos” and a fear of speaking out against the Trump administration .

Parker and Stone’s lucrative deal with Paramount over the global streaming rights to South Park includes the delivery of 50 new episodes over five seasons, with the pair agreeing to produce at least 10 new episodes of South Park a year.

articles.title: LEGO Reveals Its Biggest Book Nook Set So Far and It's Not Connected to Any Major Franchises
articles.body:
LEGO has officially revealed the LEGO Icons Bookstore: Book Nook, which is set to release on October 1. At 1,690 pieces, it's the largest book nook LEGO has released to date and is an 18+ set stacked with tiny details.

In addition to being the largest LEGO Book Nook so far, this set is also the first one completely disconnected from any sort of outside IP. There's no Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings theme attached here, just a lovely little bookstore you can fit into your own personal library.

LEGO has been getting more into book nooks since June 2025, when they released multiple sets at once. The company has had a distinct advantage over other book nook brands in that they have been able to create officially licensed sets based on popular franchises. That includes the Harry Potter Hogwarts Express book nook as well as the Lord of the Rings Balrog scene . While this new set is a departure from the usual strategy, it's more in line with what you can find in the wider book nook market.

Despite being unattached to any sort of IP, this book nook is the most expensive build so far. At $149.99, what you're mostly paying for is all of the extra pieces and subtle references to popular literature. In addition to the book nook itself, you also get two minifigures representing an author and a reader. The set isn't representative of any popular bookstores , but it does evoke the sort of classy and cozy vibe you'd expect from your local bookshop.

LEGO has released a variety of book nooks and bookends since last year, all of which are quite enjoyable to put together. I myself had the chance to build the LEGO Wicked bookends and had a blast doing it. These sets are a great example of how an adult set can be both functional and fun at the same time.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: Original Star Wars and Starfighter Heading to IMAX 70mm
articles.summary: Lucasfilm announced that the original Star Wars and Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter will get historic IMAX 70mm releases in 2027.
articles.body:
Lucasfilm and Disney announced Tuesday that the original Star Wars film from 1977 and the upcoming movie Star Wars: Starfighter will debut in IMAX 70mm in 2027.

Star Wars will be presented in IMAX for the first time to mark the classic's 50th anniversary. It will be available on digital and film when it’s re-released in theaters on February 19, 2027.

“Part of Lucasfilm’s yearlong 50th anniversary celebration, the newly restored version of the original movie, later renamed Star Wars: A New Hope, will be shown across a select number of IMAX 70mm film locations as well as playing in select theaters for a limited time,” according to StarWars.com .

Star Wars is also getting its first Welsh-language dub release for the film’s 50th anniversary next year.

Star Wars was made for the biggest screen possible. In 2027, Star Wars (1977) and Star Wars: Starfighter will release in IMAX and IMAX 70mm: pic.twitter.com/53Ca35ch5W — IMAX (@IMAX) September 8, 2026

articles.title: 'It Definitely Was a Shock': The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Artwork Splits Fans Following Trailer Reveal
articles.summary: What do you think of the new art style for Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake? It's the big question that fans have been discussing ever since today's Zelda Direct — and now they're poring over new artwork, too.
articles.body:
What do you think of the new art style for Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake? It's the big question that fans have been discussing ever since today's Zelda Direct — and now they're poring over new artwork, too.

Looking over social media commentary alongside the Direct itself, there was a fair amount of surprise at how different this version of Nintendo's N64 classic actually looked. Of course, the visuals in this ground-up Ocarina remake have been given a vast upgrade. But the visual style employed here by Nintendo looks unlike any other Zelda game seen to date.

The intent here, I think, is to create something that bridges the gap between the Switch 2's technical capability while retaining the slightly exaggerated and angular aesthetic of the N64 original. There's also a conscious decision not to turn this version of Ocarina into something it's not — a cel-shaded game, something stylized in the same fashion as Breath of the Wild, or even the grittier 3D tones of Twilight Princess.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Artwork

Of course, not everyone is a fan. "They Cocomelon'd all of them 😞," wrote one fan, examining the character artwork that Nintendo has now released via Ocarina of Time's Japanese website (check it out in the slideshow of images above). "Kid Link looks like a goldfish," wrote another.

"It's not a bad design, but I grew up with the original, so the new designs just look too busy," wrote a third, who seemed to sit more on the fence. "I think that if I wasn't so familiar with the original I might like them a bit more."

Particular criticism seems to be being levelled at Young Link and Young Zelda, who have kept some of the stylized dimensions of their N64 designs (big foreheads!) while also now appearing far more detailed.

"I hate how wet and greebled Child Link looks, the voice acting and cutscenes seem abysmal, and Kokiri Forest looks gross, but otherwise it seems kind of great," wrote one fan with strong opinions. "The sizzle reel at the end looked unbelievably good. They should've started with that."

NO IT JUST FUCKING HIT ME pic.twitter.com/NPiNDcBTI8 — CheeseGX (@CheeseGX_) September 8, 2026

NO IT JUST FUCKING HIT ME pic.twitter.com/NPiNDcBTI8

"I think part of Zeldas charm is that they always try new styles so I'd rather this than just the 3DS remake again," said another. "Zelda does look very weird though 😂"

Numerous comments mention the popular fan-made Unreal Engine projects that have popped up over the years, reimagining what Nintendo's series would look like updated to UE5. "We've been getting these UE fan remake projects for years now, and it's foolish to think Nintendo wasn't paying attention thinking this is what fans wanted," one fan added. "I think it looks good, and the cel shaded look needs a break."

"It definitely was a shock at first for me seeing it, but I appreciated the new art direction/style the more I watched it," said a more positive fan.

Is it just me, or did they make him look more like Benjamin Evan? pic.twitter.com/sk1IQg7DY7 — Gibran Teske (@gibranteske) September 8, 2026

Is it just me, or did they make him look more like Benjamin Evan? pic.twitter.com/sk1IQg7DY7

"Link (and other characters) look so adorable to me, and I like the new details such as beads on his cap," said another, clearly approving of Nintendo's new take. "Young Link looks so small and cute, we must protect him," said a third.

Of all the characters, Sheik and Ganondorf both seem to have garnered particular praise. (The less said about the Zora, the better.) "That Sheik redesign alone justifies this entire remake," said one fan. "They understood the assignment." And another: "Ganondorf looks awesome! Dude's got the aura!"

Mom said it’s my turn on the Xbox pic.twitter.com/sxcri6KrE9 — Pot Of Greed (@PotOfGreedo2) September 8, 2026

Mom said it’s my turn on the Xbox pic.twitter.com/sxcri6KrE9

Today's flurry of details included Ocarina of Time's release date , confirmation of its digital and physical pricing , details of its companion app gameplay , plus new Young Link and Young Zelda amiibo figurines . For everything else shown today, including news on the upcoming live-action Legend of Zelda movie, catch up on everything shown during the Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct right here.

articles.title: Shift Up CTO Clarifies Stellar Blade Developer's Stance on AI After Blood Rain Music Video Controversy
articles.summary: Shift Up’s chief technology officer, DongKi Lee, has clarified the developer’s stance on AI after a music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain sparked backlash last month.
articles.body:
Shift Up’s chief technology officer, DongKi Lee, has clarified the developer’s stance on AI after a music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain sparked backlash last month.

The music video, set to an upbeat pop song titled "Wanna be in Love," featured AI-generated images and footage that focused on Blood Rain’s main character, Evie, as she sang, danced, and made her way through the game’s futuristic world.

The public response was far from positive; players instantly lashed out at Shift Up for eschewing human employees in favor of having AI make the video, criticisms that the developer’s CEO, Kim Hyung Tae, argued against.

"EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work. The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and craftsmanship our team created. We would truly appreciate it if you could view the work with that understanding in mind," he wrote.

Shift Up’s CTO has now shed a bit more light on the situation now that tensions have cooled. In a September 2 interview with TheGamer , Lee explained that the company merely wanted to show off more of Evie’s world with its AI music video, and clarified that such content is "experimental" and not a reflection of the official game.

"The reason we revealed that music video was to show more of the beauty of Stellar Blade Blood Rain. We wanted to show the world view and the character Evie. We just wanted to show a little more of each, and we did that as part of the content," he began.

"But then, we do take seriously and importantly what the fans have been saying, and the concerns they have been expressing about the music video, and from now on we definitely want to make a clear separation between the two, like game-related content and what we would call experimental content, like what we are experimenting with."

Lee went on to clarify Shift Up’s stance on AI, saying that such technology should be used as a "tool" to make a good product.

"AI has a lot of influence and impact on game development. But when we are using certain technologies or tools, what's important is the direction and purpose they serve. It needs to be used in a way that supports the developers' creativity, know-how, and skills. It should be used as a tool. That's the direction, and its purpose would be to make a great, high-quality game," he said.

Unsurprisingly, the reactions from players haven’t been any more positive in light of these new comments, with the overall sentiment being that, rather than relying on AI to make a promotional music video, Shift Up could have relied on its talented employees, instead.

"'More of the beauty of Stellar Blade Blood Rain,' gang, y'all could've just animated it to show that much better," one remarked on X.

"They could have 'shown more of the beauty' by creating a music video themselves. Lol," another said .

"If they wanted to show the beauty of the game, why not just release a trailer? They definitely came up with this excuse after it caught fire," another wrote .

The use of AI in game development has been a hot-button issue over the last few years. Several titles have been at the center of this debate, including the highly-anticipated Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis , which developer Crystal Dynamics has confirmed they used AI for early prototyping, but maintained that its "finished content is human-created."

It remains unclear if Blood Rain will officially include AI, but based on Lee’s latest remarks, it seems as though Shift Up views it as a 'tool' to make a better game and support the craft and skill of its developers.

articles.title: Sega's President Says There's Been an Increase in Fans Who Don't Play Its Games, but That Doesn't Mean They Aren't Gamers
articles.summary: Sega president and COO Shuji Utsumi says the company has experienced an uptick in fans who don’t actually play the games it develops and publishes.
articles.body:
Sega president and COO Shuji Utsumi says the company has experienced an uptick in fans who don’t actually play the games it develops and publishes.

In a September 7 interview with Nikkei Gaming , Utsumi discussed the company’s current “transmedia” strategy, which has seen some of its biggest franchises — such as Sonic the Hedgehog , Persona , Yakuza , etc. — cross over into the worlds of film and television to expand their brands across multiple different mediums.

This, of course, has led to a rise in fans of these games who haven't actually played them. Utsumi confirmed this sentiment to Nikkei Gaming’s editor-in-chief, Aya Hirano, after she broached the topic by saying, “Lately, there's been an increase in fans who like an IP even though they've never played the game.”

“We've seen an increase in such fans for every title in recent years,” Utsumi answered. “For example, the Yakuza series has been doing exceptionally well in merchandising, with 60-70% of its buyers being women. They've become fans of the Yakuza world, story, and characters after watching our YouTube channel and popular YouTubers' streams. And among them are many people who have never actually played the game.”

Utsumi isn’t calling these fans LARPers, though; instead, he says that Sega considers all of its fans to be gamers, regardless of whether they’ve picked up a controller to actually play their games or not.

“Even people who have never played games are considered fans and gamers by us. Transmedia's strength lies in increasing the entry points and contact points for people to become interested in IP. In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play the games,” he added.

Utsumi went on to explain that the rise of female fans within the gaming space has created a shift in the types of merchandise that publishers produce, specifically calling back to his experience working at Cybird, a developer famous for its Otome romance games.

“I also worked on romance games for women at Cybird. There, in addition to traditional collectible goods such as can badges and acrylic stands, we saw a significant shift in merchandising, with the emergence of lifestyle-oriented licensed products like apparel and cosmetics that could be used daily, as well as limited-edition and commemorative goods created in collaboration with amusement facilities. That experience definitely broadened my perspective, and I believe it's been invaluable in my transmedia strategy at Sega,” he said.

Sega’s “transmedia” strategy is clearly working out for it, with all three live-action Sonic movies making bank at the box office and a fourth to come — not to mention the upcoming Persona series that’s in the works at Netflix. Whether or not these projects’ popularity translates to more players seems moot to Sega, though. To them, every fan is a “gamer” at heart.

articles.title: Nintendo Intentionally Included Loading Screens in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and Fans Are Torn
articles.summary: Nintendo has confirmed it intentionally included loading screens in its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake to "preserve the essence of the original game," and the internet isn't in love with the idea.
articles.body:
Nintendo has confirmed that it intentionally included loading screens in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake to "preserve the essence of the original game," and the internet isn't in love with the idea.

Confirmation that loading screens would cut into the remake's playtime arrived during a gameplay demonstration shown as part of today's The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct . It's an extremely brief moment that saw series producer Eiji Aonuma confirm that the Ocarina of Time remake will channel the power of the Nintendo 64 when it launches for Nintendo Switch 2 this November.

"By the way, there's a loading screen whenever you move between areas," Aonuma said as Link and Navi traveled from Kokiri Forest to Hyrule Field. "This is something we intentionally kept to preserve the essence of the original game."

Let's take a second to break down the footage. In the 1998 Ocarina of Time , as well as so many other games before and after it, loading screens allowed developers to pause the experience and load new areas for the player to explore. With the exception of some cutscenes before and after the original transition between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field, players really only had control of Link taken away for a few seconds.

The Ocarina of Time remake appears to be a bit more seamless. It's unclear if Aonuma's demo will play out the same as the full release, but here, we see the player in control of Link before a black screen consumes the visuals. It and a small Triforce logo in the bottom right corner are on-screen for about three seconds before Young Link trots back into view.

Massive changes to the art style aside, Nintendo's decision to "preserve the essence" of 1998's groundbreaking adventure game seems to mostly line up. That said, in the nearly 30 years since that game came out, players have adapted to an advancing industry that often attempts to hide its loading screens – and that's if a game has them, at all.

Nintendo intentionally left some loading screen sections in the Ocarina of Time Remake to preserve the feel of the OG. pic.twitter.com/JBRtLfitq4 — Kabi (@KabiPlays) September 8, 2026

Nintendo intentionally left some loading screen sections in the Ocarina of Time Remake to preserve the feel of the OG. pic.twitter.com/JBRtLfitq4

Choosing to intentionally include loading screens in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has players split. While some love the idea of a reimagining that pays homage to '90s N64 gaming, others see the breaks between gameplay as not only a silly addition but a confusing one, too. Some even suspect Nintendo included the loading screens because it needed them on the Switch 2, and not because it wanted them.

"Loading times in to preserve feel?" one fan said . "Lol I don't believe that for a second. It's fine that they are in there but don't say that's why you did it, Nintendo."

"'Loading times/screen still in the game between areas, added intentional to preserve feel of the game,' I'm sorry, what? Lmao," one fan said . "That's stupid."

"I didn’t mind that," another argued . "It makes the areas feel more apart and contrasted. That and also the loading screens are two seconds, so who gives a s**t."

“The loading screen is intentional to keep the nostalgia of the original game” Legend of Zelda direct making me laugh pic.twitter.com/9yKxMKNZav — ducky (@duckyjrtwitch) September 8, 2026

“The loading screen is intentional to keep the nostalgia of the original game” Legend of Zelda direct making me laugh pic.twitter.com/9yKxMKNZav

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5, 2026. It'll have more than redone load screens when it arrives, with players also still coming to grips with the wild changes Nintendo made to the game's visuals .
